title: Electromagnetic Induction — 60 MCQs
description: Faraday's & Lenz's laws, AC generators, eddy currents, self/mutual inductance, energy in inductors, transformers and losses. Questions range from basic concepts to advanced applications.

questions.q: Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction states the induced emf in a closed circuit equals:
options: Negative rate of change of magnetic flux through the circuit
Positive rate of change of charge
Integral of electric field along open path
questions.explanation: Faraday: ε = − dΦ/dt (flux linkage change). Negative sign indicates Lenz's law.

questions.q: The negative sign in Faraday's law corresponds to which principle?
options: Lenz's law (induced emf opposes flux change)
questions.explanation: Lenz's law gives direction such that induced current opposes change in flux — represented by minus sign.

questions.q: Lenz's law ensures the induced current direction is such that it:
options: Opposes the change in magnetic flux that produced it
questions.explanation: Lenz's law enforces conservation of energy by opposing the cause of induction.

questions.q: If the magnetic flux through a loop increases into the page, the induced current will produce a magnetic field:
options: Out of the page to oppose increase
Into the page to help increase
questions.explanation: To oppose increasing into-page flux, induced field must be out of page; use right-hand rule to set current direction.

questions.q: A coil of N turns is rotated in a uniform magnetic field with angular frequency ω. The peak induced emf amplitude is:
options: N B A ω (for area A)
questions.explanation: If angle between normal and B varies as ωt, emf amplitude = N B A ω (sinusoids give max N B A ω).

questions.q: If a rectangular loop moves out of a uniform magnetic field region, the induced emf appears because:
options: Magnetic flux through loop changes with time
questions.explanation: Flux change (due to area in field changing) induces emf per Faraday.

questions.q: Motional emf produced when a conductor of length l moves with velocity v perpendicular to B is:
questions.explanation: Motional emf from v × B acting on charges across length: ε = B l v (for perpendicular orientation).

questions.q: A conductor moves parallel to B (no component perpendicular). The motional emf is:
questions.explanation: If v parallel to B then cross product zero so no motional emf.

questions.q: An induced emf in a closed loop can be produced by:
options: Changing magnetic field, changing area of loop, or changing orientation of loop
questions.explanation: Flux changes can occur by varying B, A, or angle between B and area vector.

questions.q: If magnetic flux through a coil changes sinusoidally with time, the induced emf is:
options: Sinusoidal and phase-shifted by 90° relative to flux
questions.explanation: Emf = -dΦ/dt; derivative of sine is cosine (90° phase shift).

questions.q: A single-turn loop and a 10-turn coil experience identical flux change ΔΦ. The induced charge magnitude passing during change is:
questions.explanation: Total induced emf ∝ N; for same rate, more turns produce greater total emf and integrated charge (assuming same resistance per turn aggregate).

questions.q: When a bar magnet is pushed quickly into a coil, the induced current in coil will:
options: Oppose the motion of the magnet (magnetic braking)
Help the magnet to move faster
questions.explanation: Induced currents create fields opposing the change; work must be done to push magnet, appearing as mechanical resistance.

questions.q: Eddy currents are:
options: Circulating currents induced in bulk conductors by changing magnetic flux
questions.explanation: Eddy currents are loops inside conductors; cause heating and magnetic damping.

questions.q: An example where eddy currents are useful is:
options: Eddy-current braking in trains and metal detectors
questions.explanation: Eddy currents are exploited for non-contact braking and for detecting conductive objects.

questions.q: An example where eddy currents are a nuisance is:
options: Heating and energy loss in transformer cores if not laminated
questions.explanation: Eddy currents in solid cores cause significant I^2R losses; cores are laminated to reduce them.

questions.q: To reduce eddy current losses in a transformer core you:
options: Use laminated core or high-resistivity core materials
Use a solid thick iron block
questions.explanation: Lamination increases electrical resistance of current paths, reducing eddy currents.

questions.q: Self-inductance L of a coil is defined by relation:
options: Φ = L I (flux linkage proportional to current)
questions.explanation: Inductance relates flux linkage to current; L depends on coil geometry and medium.

questions.q: Mutual inductance M between two coils means:
options: Flux in one coil due to current in the other per unit current
questions.explanation: M = Φ21 / I1 (flux through coil 2 due to current I1) assuming linearity; symmetric property M12=M21.

questions.q: Mutual inductance M between two coils depends on:
options: Number of turns, geometry and magnetic coupling (core/permeability)
questions.explanation: Mutual coupling determined by how well flux from one links the other and by turns.

questions.q: A key use of mutual inductance is in:
questions.explanation: Transformers use mutual inductance to transfer energy between circuits at different voltages.

questions.q: Energy stored in an inductor with inductance L carrying current I is:
questions.explanation: Magnetic energy stored in inductor = 1/2 L I².

questions.q: If current in an inductor changes rapidly, voltage across it is v = L (dI/dt). This property is called:
questions.explanation: An inductor resists change in current; induced emf = L dI/dt.

questions.q: Inductive reactance X_L of an inductor in AC circuit is:
questions.explanation: Inductive reactance increases with frequency; X_L = 2π f L.

questions.q: In an ideal inductor the current lags the applied voltage by:
options: 90° (π/2) in a purely inductive AC circuit
questions.explanation: Voltage leads current by 90° in ideal inductance (v = L di/dt).

questions.q: Back emf in an inductor opposes change of current according to:
options: Lenz's law and v = L dI/dt
questions.explanation: Induced emf opposes change in current (Lenz), magnitude L dI/dt.

questions.q: If two inductors are connected in series with coupling coefficient k, total inductance is:
options: L_total = L1 + L2 ± 2 M (depending on connection)
questions.explanation: Mutual inductance adds or subtracts depending on aiding or opposing orientation; M = k sqrt(L1 L2).

questions.q: Coupling coefficient k ranges between:
questions.explanation: k = M / sqrt(L1 L2), limited to [0,1] for non-pathological cases.

questions.q: A coil wound on an iron core has larger inductance than same coil in air because:
options: Higher permeability of core concentrates flux and increases L
questions.explanation: Magnetic core increases flux linkage per current, increasing inductance.

questions.q: Self inductance of a solenoid of N turns, length l, cross-sectional area A is approximately:
options: L ≈ μ0 μ_r N² A / l
questions.explanation: Inductance of long solenoid: L = μ N² A / l where μ = μ0 μ_r.

questions.q: When current in primary coil changes, induced emf in secondary equals:
questions.explanation: Φ2 = M I1, so emf in coil2 = − dΦ2/dt = − M dI1/dt.

questions.q: A simple AC generator (alternator) produces emf by:
options: Rotating coil in a magnetic field producing time-varying flux linkage
Sliding magnet across coil only DC
questions.explanation: AC generator: coil rotates in B producing sinusoidal flux change and induced emf.

questions.q: Output emf of ideal AC generator with N turns, area A, B field, rotating at ω is:
options: ε(t) = N B A ω sin(ω t) (or cosine depending on reference)
questions.explanation: Flux = N B A cos(ωt); ε = − dΦ/dt = N B A ω sin(ωt).

questions.q: Slip rings in an AC generator are used to:
options: Provide continuous connection to rotating coil while delivering AC
questions.explanation: Slip rings maintain electrical contact to rotating coil for AC output; brushes slide on rings.

questions.q: Commutator is used in DC machines to:
options: Convert induced alternating emf in coils to unidirectional output
questions.explanation: Commutator (split ring) reverses connection each half rotation to produce DC from rotating coil.

questions.q: In an AC generator, maximum power transfer to a purely resistive load occurs when load is:
options: Purely resistive and matched to generator internal impedance for maximum power point
questions.explanation: Maximum power transfer occurs when load equals internal source impedance (for complex sources matching both R and reactive parts).

questions.q: When flux through a stationary coil is changed by a time-varying current in nearby coil, the phenomenon is:
questions.explanation: Changing current in one coil induces emf in nearby coil via mutual inductance.

questions.q: If mutual inductance between two coils is M and the rate of change of current in coil1 is dI1/dt, induced emf in coil2 magnitude equals:
questions.explanation: Emf magnitude = M times absolute rate of change; sign determined by Lenz's law.

questions.q: A transformer transfers power between circuits most efficiently when:
options: Its core has high permeability and is laminated to reduce eddy currents
questions.explanation: High μ concentrates flux and lamination limits eddy currents, increasing efficiency.

questions.q: Ideal transformer equations (turns N1,N2) relate voltages by:
options: V2/V1 = N2/N1 and I1/I2 = N2/N1 (for ideal, power conserved)
questions.explanation: Ideal transformer: voltage ratio equals turns ratio; current ratio inversely so power approximately conserved ignoring losses.

questions.q: In a step-up transformer the secondary has:
options: More turns than primary and higher voltage
questions.explanation: Step-up increases voltage by increasing turns N2 > N1.

questions.q: Energy stored in magnetic field of inductor is recovered when current decreases; this energy originally came from:
options: Work done by source to establish the current against induced emf
questions.explanation: Energy stored in magnetic field equals work done to build current against back emf.

questions.q: Transformer core hysteresis loss depends mainly on:
options: Area of B–H loop and frequency of magnetization
questions.explanation: Hysteresis loss per cycle ∝ loop area; total loss increases with frequency.

questions.q: Other principal transformer losses include:
options: Eddy current loss in core, copper loss in windings, flux leakage and stray losses
questions.explanation: Transformers lose energy via core eddy currents, winding I²R (copper) losses, leakage flux, dielectric and stray losses.

questions.q: Eddy current loss in transformer core increases with:
options: Square of frequency and square of flux density (approx)
questions.explanation: Eddy current loss ~ k_e f² B_m² for simple models; lamination reduces it.

questions.q: Copper loss in transformer windings is proportional to:
options: I² R (load current squared times winding resistance)
questions.explanation: I²R loss in windings increases with square of current and winding resistance.

questions.q: Open-circuit test on a transformer is used to measure primarily:
options: Core losses and magnetizing current (hysteresis and eddy losses)
questions.explanation: OC test applies rated voltage with secondary open to observe no-load current and core losses.

questions.q: Short-circuit test on a transformer is used to determine:
options: Copper losses and equivalent series impedance
questions.explanation: SC test applies reduced voltage to cause rated current and measures I²R (copper) losses and leakage reactance.

questions.q: Leakage flux in transformer is undesired because it:
options: Does not link both windings and reduces coupling, causing leakage reactance
questions.explanation: Leakage flux contributes to series leakage reactance limiting short-circuit current and voltage regulation.

questions.q: Power transformer efficiency improves when:
options: Core and copper losses are minimized and proper loading is maintained
questions.explanation: Efficiency high when losses small relative to output; design and load factor influence losses and efficiency.

questions.q: Autotransformer differs from two-winding transformer by:
options: Sharing a portion of winding between primary and secondary (single continuous winding)
questions.explanation: Autotransformer uses tapped single winding; economical but no full isolation.

questions.q: If primary of ideal transformer has N1 turns and secondary N2 turns, flux per turn Φ is determined by applied voltage V1 and frequency f by:
options: V1 = 4.44 f N1 Φ_m (for sinusoidal peak values)
Flux independent of V1 and f
questions.explanation: RMS voltage V = 4.44 f N Φ_m for sinusoidal flux amplitude Φ_m; used in transformer design.

questions.q: If frequency in transformer is reduced (with same applied voltage), flux in core will:
questions.explanation: V ∝ f Φ, so lower f increases flux for same V; core design must account for frequency to avoid saturation.

questions.q: Core saturation in transformer leads to:
options: Distortion of waveform, high magnetizing current and heating
questions.explanation: Saturation reduces permeability causing nonlinear magnetization, increased magnetizing current and distortion.

questions.q: A single-phase AC generator output frequency depends on:
options: Number of poles and rotation speed (f = (P/2) * (rpm/60))
questions.explanation: Electrical frequency determined by mechanical rotation speed and pole pairs.

questions.q: In eddy-current dampers used in meters, the damping force is proportional to:
options: Velocity of moving conductor in field (v) and B² and geometry
questions.explanation: Eddy currents proportional to rate of change of flux (velocity) and produce damping force ∝ v.

questions.q: A rotating loop in a magnetic field that produces emf also experiences a torque resisting rotation. This torque is due to:
options: Lenz's law: induced currents produce fields opposing motion (generator reaction)
questions.explanation: Mechanical input must do work against electromagnetic torque; energy converted to electrical form.

questions.q: In a transformer's iron core, adding silicon to the iron alloy primarily:
options: Reduces hysteresis loss by increasing resistivity and altering magnetic properties
questions.explanation: Silicon steel reduces core losses by decreasing hysteresis and eddy currents via higher resistivity.

questions.q: For an ideal lossless transformer, input and output power are related by:
options: V1 I1 cosφ1 = V2 I2 cosφ2 (power in = power out ignoring losses)
questions.explanation: Ideal transformer conserves real power (accounting for phase), V1I1 = V2I2 if phase same; often simplified for resistive loads.

questions.q: A clamp-on iron-core device that uses induction to detect current in a conductor is called:
questions.explanation: CT uses magnetic coupling to sense current in primary conductor via transformer action.

questions.q: Lenz's law and Faraday's law together guarantee conservation of energy because:
options: Induced emf opposes change, so work must be done to change flux; electrical energy comes from mechanical work
They create energy out of nothing
questions.explanation: Opposing induced currents require input work; energy converted consistently between mechanical and electrical forms.
